description: The core component of the Linux operating system that acts as a bridge between the software applications and the hardware.
Bourne Again SHell, the default command-line interpreter (CLI) in most Linux distributions.
Stands for 'Superuser DO'. A command that allows permitted users to execute a command as the superuser or another user.
The administrative user account in Linux that has absolute privileges and access to all files and commands on the system.
Short for 'distribution'. A specific version of the Linux operating system packaged with different software, desktop environments, and package managers (e.g., Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian).
A computer program that runs as a background process, rather than being under the direct control of an interactive user. Usually ends with the letter 'd' (e.g., systemd, sshd).
A system and service manager for Linux that acts as an init system to bootstrap the user space and manage system processes after booting.
Advanced Package Tool. The default package manager used by Debian and Ubuntu-based Linux distributions for installing, updating, and removing software.
Yellowdog Updater, Modified. A command-line package-management utility for computers running compatible versions of Linux, mainly RHEL and CentOS.
A time-based job scheduler in Unix-like operating systems used to schedule scripts or commands to run automatically at specified intervals.
A command-line utility used to search plain-text data sets for lines that match a specific regular expression or string.
Change Mode. A command used to change the access permissions (read, write, execute) of files and directories.
Change Owner. A command used to change the user owner and group owner of a file or directory.
Secure Shell. A cryptographic network protocol used to securely access and manage a computer over an unsecured network.
A data structure on a Linux filesystem that stores all metadata about a file (permissions, owner, size) except for its actual name and data content.
Symbolic Link. A special type of file that serves as a reference or shortcut to another file or directory, similar to a shortcut in Windows.
Tape Archive. A command-line utility used to collect many files into one archive file (a tarball) for easy distribution or backup.
Command-Line Interface. A text-based user interface used to view and manage computer files and interact with the operating system.
Graphical User Interface. The visual way of interacting with a computer using items such as windows, icons, and menus.
Print Working Directory. A command that outputs the absolute path of the current directory you are in.
A command used to send a specific signal to a process, most commonly used to force-stop or terminate an unresponsive application.
Short for 'manual'. A command used to display the user manual of any command that we can run on the terminal.
